summary: Daniel Veidlinger works in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago under Steven Collins, also studying under Samli Mulkæo and Nalini Devdas. He held posts at Chiang Mai University (1999) and California State University, Chico (2003).

Daniel W. Kent is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Virginia and was an instructor at both the University of Virginia and Mary Baldwin University (attested 2010).

Daniel Wojahn works in Tibetology and history and archaeology. He studied at Leipzig (MA, 2013–2016) and Oxford (DPhil, 2019–2024). His roles include posts at Leipzig, Brill, Oxford, Bonn (2024), and an associate researcher position at Vienna (2025).

Daniel Wright (1833–1902) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of St Andrews (~1851–1855) and served as a physician at the British Residency in Nepal from 1866 to 1876.

Daniela Berti specializes in Indology and religious studies. She studied at Sapienza University of Rome, the University of Siena (PhD), and Paris Nanterre University (HDR). She has held posts at INALCO (2001–2003), Milieux, Cultures et Sociétés en Himalaya, and CNRS.

Daniela Bevilacqua works in Indology and religious studies. She studied at Sapienza University of Rome (2002–2005) and earned a PhD at Paris Nanterre University. She held posts at SOAS (2015–2020), University of Turin (2021), and Iscte – University Institute of Lisbon (2023).

Daniela De Simone works in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. She studied at Kendriya Hindi Sansthan, LSE, and the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (PhD 2007–2012). Her posts include the British Museum (2016–2020) and Ghent University (2021).
Daniele Cuneo has taught at the University of Paris and the Sorbonne (attested 2018). He was also appointed to the faculty at the University of Texas at Austin (attested 2026).
Danielle Feller is an Indologist who completed her PhD at the University of Lausanne in 2001 under the supervision of Johannes Bronkhorst. She also studied under Ganesh U. Thite.
Danny M.C. Ching is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and sinology. He has been a PhD student at Columbia University, attested in 2023 and 2026.
Danping Long works in Indology and Buddhist studies. She is a doctoral student associated with the University of Munich and the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2026).

Danuta Stasik is an Indologist who studied at the University of Warsaw (~1975–1980) under Maria Byrski. She joined the faculty at the University of Warsaw in 1986, serving as Chair of South Asian Studies in the Faculty of Oriental Studies.

Daoquan Yu (1901–1992) worked in Tibetology and linguistics. He studied at Cheeloo University (~1920–1924) and under Jacques Bacot (~1934–1937), and served as a professor at Minzu University of China from approximately 1953 to 1992.

Dasharatha Sharma (1903–1976) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied at the University of Delhi. He held posts at Hindu College, Delhi University (~1960–1969), Jai Narain Vyas University (1966), and the Rajasthan Oriental Research Institute.

Daud Ali is an Indologist and historian. He studied at William & Mary and the University of Chicago under Ronald Inden. He taught history at SOAS (~1995–2008) and became an associate professor at the University of Pennsylvania in 2009.
David A. Dilworth works in philosophy and Japanology. He studied under Masao Abe and Valdo H. Viglielmo (1968).

David A. Hall works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied under Shoshin Ichishima (1976) and earned a doctorate at UC Berkeley (1990). He was a visiting scholar at Taisho University (1977) and department chair at Montgomery College (attested 2019).

David Aberle (1918–2004) studied at Harvard University (~1937–1940), Columbia University (~1941–1950), and the University of New Mexico. He held an academic post at the University of British Columbia from approximately 1967 to 1983.
David Azzopardi works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at SOAS University of London, where he completed his PhD under the supervision of Kate Crosby (attested 2010).

David B. Gray works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology. He completed his Ph.D. at Columbia University under Robert A. F. Thurman. He held posts as a postdoctoral fellow at Rice University and assistant professor at Santa Clara University (attested 2005–2017).
